subject: Exploring data curation & annotation for AStuff’s off-road autonomy projects
text:
Hi [NAME],

We recently started working with Ouster on improving quality assurance for
their LiDAR labels, which is how I came across [COMPANY].

We partner with teams across the off-road autonomy space (from John Deere
and Overland AI to Anduril) as well as self-driving and ADAS groups at
Woven by Toyota, Otiv, and Nexar.

For off-road systems in particular, we've helped teams mine and surface
edge-case data (e.g. desert terrain, fog, low-light conditions) to
prioritise for annotation and model retraining.

Would you be open to a short chat or demo to see where Encord could fit
into AStuff's 2D and 3D ML stack? If nothing else, would be great to get
your candid feedback on what we've built and for you to see what is out
there.

subject: Multimodal Dinner - SF - 30 Oct
text:
Hi [NAME],

Our founder [SENDER] is hosting a small dinner in SF on Thursday, 30th
October at Spruce. I'd love to extend an invite.

The evening's theme is the multimodal shift in AI - the convergence of
vision, language and sensor data for autonomous systems. We're keeping it
small (c.20 guests), mostly heads of AI/ technical leaders joining from
teams e.g. 1X, the Bot Company, Glydways etc. I thought you might enjoy
being part of the discussions.

For context - Encord supports leading physical AI teams (e.g. Boston
Dynamics, Woven by Toyota & Physical Intelligence) automate their
annotation pipelines at scale + unify image, video and point cloud data
development in one place.

Happy to share the full event details if you can make it?

subject: Follow-up on labeling setup Adam mentioned
text:
Hi [NAME],

Shame we missed each other at Actuate, but I managed to catch-up with Adam,
and he mentioned you currently insource labelling due to the US-based
workforce requirement and that 2D tools like CVAT have been sufficient so
far.

We've onboarded 1X last week (alongside Boston Dynamics earlier this year)
to help their perception teams move past those same CVAT-style limitations,
especially for captioning and multimodal tasks like vision-language
alignment and QA. They've been able to keep control of their data while
improving throughput and label quality.

Would it make sense to share how they approached it and where Encord fits
into their ML pipeline? Even if you're continuing to insource, it might
give you a few ideas for scaling your perception and evaluation workflows.

subject: 1X & Boston Dynamics - how we helped robotics teams move beyond CVAT
text:
Hi [NAME],

I met Adam at Actuate, and he mentioned you currently insource labelling
due to the US-based workforce requirement and use 2D tools like CVAT.

We've onboarded 1X last week (alongside Boston Dynamics earlier this year)
to help their perception teams move past CVAT's limitations i.e.
inefficiencies of splitting out frames and struggling with rich captions.
We've allowed
them to keep control of their data while improving throughput and label
quality.

I'd like to show you our approach to saving them money while their models
achieve incremental gains. Even if you're continuing to insource, it might
give you a few ideas for scaling your perception and evaluation workflows.

Does next week work? We're pretty free in the afternoons.

text:

missed you.

reasoning work.

see if it aligns with your team's needs moving forward?
